- graph_debug: 对比 NPU 图模式(cudagraph)与单算子模式(enforce-eager)精度。预分配 buffer + 异步 copy_ 记录中间 tensor，model runner 中统一写文件对比。
- skill-creator-0.1.0: Guide for creating effective skills. This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends Claude's capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations.
- ssh-skill: CRITICAL: Use this skill for ALL SSH/server operations. NEVER run raw ssh/scp directly. Triggers: SSH, remote server, server IP/hostname/user@host, connect/login, run command on server, check server/status, deploy, upload/download, file transfer, bastion/jump host, server-to-server transfer, migrate, tunnel, port forward, database/internal service access, and Chinese terms: 服务器, 远程, 连接, 登录, 上传, 下载, 部署, 跳板机, 服务器间传输, 迁移, 隧道, 端口转发, 数据库连接, 内网访问. Provides persistent connections, pooling, jump hosts, SFTP, tunneling, and recovery. DO NOT use for local commands, localhost, or current-directory work.
- vllm-ascend-developer: vLLM/vLLM-Ascend 通用开发 skill，覆盖精度诊断、服务管理、测试验证等场景，支持单机/PD分离双模式
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

1	# vLLM Ascend Development Guidelines
2	
3	This document provides instructions for contributors to the vLLM Ascend project. Please read and follow these guidelines to ensure code quality, maintainability, and consistency.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Table of Contents
8	
9	- [Setup and Environment](#setup-and-environment)
10	    - [Environment Variables](#environment-variables)
11	    - [Environment Variable Review Requirement](#environment-variable-review-requirement)
12	- [Testing](#testing)
13	    - [Unit and System Tests](#unit-and-system-tests)
14	    - [Running Tests](#running-tests)
15	- [Code Style](#code-style)
16	    - [Python Conventions](#python-conventions)
17	    - [Naming Conventions](#naming-conventions)
18	- [NPU-Specific Considerations](#npu-specific-considerations)
19	    - [Tensor item() Operations](#tensor-item-operations)
20	    - [Memory and Performance](#memory-and-performance)
21	- [Model and Plugin Architecture](#model-and-plugin-architecture)
22	    - [vLLM Ascend Plugin Architecture](#vllm-ascend-plugin-architecture)
23	    - [Patching Requirement](#patching-requirement)
24	    - [Model Runner Changes](#model-runner-changes)
25	- [Commit Messages and Pull Requests](#commit-messages-and-pull-requests)
26	    - [Commit Message Format](#commit-message-format)
27	- [Review Checklist](#review-checklist)
28	    - [Code Quality](#code-quality)
29	    - [Testing](#testing-1)
30	    - [Documentation](#documentation)
31	    - [NPU Considerations](#npu-considerations)
32	    - [Commit and PR](#commit-and-pr)
33	- [Quick Start for Contributors](#quick-start-for-contributors)
34	- [References](#references)
35	
36	---
37	
38	## Setup and Environment
39	
40	### Environment Variables
41	
42	All environment variables must be defined in `vllm_ascend/envs.py` using the centralized `env_variables` dictionary.
43	
44	**Requirements:**
45	
46	- Add documentation for each environment variable in the `env_variables` dict comment
47	- Specify default values and valid ranges
48	- Indicate whether the variable is sensitive (credentials, keys)
49	
50	**Example:**
51	
52	```python
53	import os
54	
55	env_variables = {
56	    "VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_NZ": lambda: int(os.getenv("VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_NZ", 1)),
57	    # ...
58	}
59	```
60	
61	**Never**: Hardcode environment variable names throughout the codebase. Reference them from the central module using `from vllm_ascend import envs`.
62	
63	### Environment Variable Review Requirement
64	
65	**Strict Review Required**: All new environment variables must undergo code review.
66	
67	Reviewers must verify:
68	
69	- The variable name follows the `VLLM_ASCEND_*` naming convention
70	- Default value is appropriate for all supported hardware
71	- Documentation is added to the `env_variables` dict
72	- The variable is used in a performance-critical path
73	
74	---
75	
76	## Testing
77	
78	### Unit and System Tests
79	
80	**Requirement**: All new functionality requires corresponding tests.
81	
82	- **Unit Tests (UT)**: Located in `tests/ut/`, cover core logic, edge cases, and error conditions
83	- **System Tests (ST)**: Located in `tests/e2e/`, verify end-to-end behavior and integration points
84	- **Nightly Tests**: Include benchmarks for NPU-specific code paths in `tests/e2e/nightly/`
85	
86	**Test Coverage Guidelines:**
87	
88	- New features: Tests must cover happy path and failure modes
89	- Bug fixes: Tests must include a regression test for the bug
90	- Performance-critical code: Include benchmarks and performance regression tests
91	
92	### Running Tests
93	
94	```bash
95	
96	
97	# Run specific unit test file
98	pytest -sv tests/ut/ops/test_prepare_finalize.py
99	
100	# Run specific unit test
101	pytest -sv tests/ut/ops/test_prepare_finalize.py::test_prepare_inputs
102	
103	# Run NPU-specific tests (requires NPU hardware)
104	pytest -sv tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/aclgraph/test_aclgraph_accuracy.py::test_default_full_and_piecewise_res_consistency
105	```
106	
107	**Requirement**: Run all tests locally before requesting review. Verify tests pass on NPU hardware for NPU-specific changes.
108	
109	---
110	
111	## Code Style
112	
113	### Python Conventions
114	
115	- **Imports**: All imports at the top of the file. Valid exceptions:
116	    - Circular imports (use inline imports)
117	    - Lazy loading for worker/isolation processes
118	    - Type-checking imports wrapped in `if TYPE_CHECKING:`
119	
120	- **Global Variables**: Avoid new global variables. Pass dependencies explicitly through function parameters.
121	
122	    **Allowed:**
123	    - Constants named `ALL_UPPER_CASE` (e.g., `MAX_BATCH_SIZE` in `envs.py`)
124	    - Immutable configuration objects
125	
126	    **Requires Approval:**
127	    - Any new mutable global state
128	
129	- **No Magic Numbers**: Use named constants with descriptive names:
130	
131	    ```python
132	    # Bad
133	    if seq_len > 2048: ...
134	
135	    # Good
136	    MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH = 2048
137	    if seq_len > MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH: ...
138	    ```
139	
140	- **Descriptive Naming**: Use names that describe functionality, not implementation details.
141	
142	    ```python
143	    # Bad
144	    is_deepseek_v3_r1
145	    flag1
146	    tmp_var
147	
148	    # Good
149	    supports_dynamic_temperature
150	    uses_speculative_decoding
151	    ```
152	
153	### Naming Conventions
154	
155	- **Classes**: `PascalCase` (e.g., `NPUModelRunner`, `AscendSampler`, `ACLGraphManager`)
156	- **Functions/Methods**: `snake_case` (e.g., `forward_pass`, `compute_attention`)
157	- **Constants**: `ALL_UPPER_CASE` (e.g., `MAX_BATCH_SIZE`, `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_NZ`)
158	- **Variables**: `snake_case` (e.g., `token_ids`, `sequence_lengths`)
159	
160	---
161	
162	## NPU-Specific Considerations
163	
164	### Tensor item() Operations
165	
166	**Warning**: `tensor.item()` operations cause synchronization overhead on NPU when the `tensor` is on device.
167	
168	If the `tensor` is a device tensor, calling `item()` will triggers a synchronous data transfer from NPU to CPU. This can severely degrade performance in hot paths, causing `AsyncScheduler` to block here.
169	
170	**Review Requirements:**
171	
172	1. Profile performance impact before merging
173	2. Consider alternative patterns:
174	    - Keep values on device when possible
175	    - Batch operations to reduce sync frequency
176	    - Use device-side operations (e.g., `torch.argmax`, `torch.sum`)
177	3. Document when `item()` is unavoidable (e.g., logging, conditional logic)
178	
179	**Example Patterns:**
180	
181	```python
182	# Bad: In hot loop - causes sync per iteration
183	for tensor in tensors:
184	    value = tensor.item()
185	
186	# Better: Batch operations - single sync
187	values = [t.item() for t in tensors]  # Single batch sync
188	
189	# Good: Keep on device when possible
190	max_value = torch.max(tensor)  # No sync needed
191	if max_value > threshold:  # Comparison can stay on device
192	    ...
193	```
194	
195	### Memory and Performance
196	
197	Additional NPU-specific best practices:
198	
199	- Avoid CPU-NPU memory transfers in hot paths
200	- Prefer in-place operations where safe (e.g., `x.add_()`, `x.mul_()`)
201	- Monitor memory fragmentation, especially for long-running processes
202	- Test with realistic workloads on actual NPU hardware (Ascend 910B/C)
203	
204	---
205	
206	## Model and Plugin Architecture
207	
208	### vLLM Ascend Plugin Architecture
209	
210	vLLM Ascend is a **hardware plugin** that integrates with upstream vLLM via the pluggable hardware interface. It does not add new model files directly.
211	
212	**Required Pattern**: Model-specific functionality should be implemented via:
213	
214	1. **Patching** (in `vllm_ascend/patch/`):
215	    - `vllm_ascend/patch/platform/` - Platform-level patches (distributed, scheduling)
216	    - `vllm_ascend/patch/worker/` - Worker-level patches (model-specific behavior)
217	    - Example: `patch_deepseek.py` modifies upstream Deepseek model behavior
218	    - Patch is not the best solution for all cases. Use it when necessary.
219	
220	2. **Inheritance**:
221	    - `NPUModelRunner(GPUModelRunner)` - Extend vLLM model runner with NPU-specific behavior
222	    - `AscendSampler` - Extend vLLM sampler with NPU-specific operations
223	    - Add NPU-specific components via composition (e.g., `AclGraphManager`)
224	    - Custom Operators - NPU-specific custom operators (e.g., `AscendRMSNorm`)
225	
226	3. **External upstream contributions** where appropriate
227	
228	### Patching Requirement
229	
230	**Strict Review Required**: All new patches must undergo thorough architectural review.
231	
232	Reviewers must verify:
233	
234	- The patch targets the correct upstream component
235	- The patch is minimal and focused
236	- Performance implications are understood
237	- A long-term plan exists for upstream contribution
238	
239	**Example Patch Pattern:**
240	
241	```python
242	# vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_deepseek.py
243	from vllm.model_executor.models.deepseek_v2 import DeepseekV2Model
244	
245	def forward(self, input_ids, positions, ...):
246	    # NPU-specific forward implementation
247	    ...
248	
249	DeepseekV2Model.forward = forward  # Patch upstream class
250	```
251	
252	### Model Runner Changes
253	
254	**Strict Review Required**: All new behaviors added to `model_runner` must undergo thorough architectural review.
255	
256	Reviewers must verify:
257	
258	- The necessity of the new behavior (why can't this be in a patch?)
259	- Performance implications on NPU hardware
260	- Compatibility with existing model implementations
261	- Long-term maintainability and test coverage
262	
263	**NPU Model Runner Files:**
264	
265	- `vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py` - vLLM v1 model runner
266	- `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py` - vLLM v2 model runner
267	- `vllm_ascend/_310p/model_runner_310p.py` - Ascend 310P model runner
268	
269	---
270	
271	## Commit Messages and Pull Requests
272	
273	### Commit Message Format
274	
275	Follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format and **must include a sign-off**:
276	
277	```bash
278	git commit -s -m "<type>: <summary>" -m "<body - explaining what changed and why>"
279	```
280	
281	Or using the full message format:
282	
283	```txt
284	<type>: <summary>
285	
286	<body - explaining what changed and why>
287	
288	Signed-off-by: Your Name <your.email@example.com>
289	```
290	
291	**Valid Types**: `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `refactor`, `test`, `docs`, `chore`
292	
293	**Good Examples:**
294	
295	```txt
296	feat(npu): add flash attention support for Ascend CANN
297	
298	- Implements FlashAttention-2 kernel for NPU backend
299	- Reduces memory usage by 30% compared to baseline
300	
301	fix(model_runner): correct padding token handling
302	
303	- Fixes token padding that caused incorrect attention masks
304	- Addresses issue #1234
305	
306	perf: avoid CPU-NPU sync in attention computation
307	
308	- Inline computation to avoid tensor.item() calls
309	- Improves throughput by 15%
310	```
311	
312	**Bad Examples:**
313	
314	```txt
315	fix bug
316	add feature
317	update code
318	```
319	
320	### Pull Request Title Format
321	
322	PR titles should follow the format: `[Type][Module] Description`
323	
324	- **Type**: The type of change (e.g., `CI`, `Doc`, `BugFix`, `Feat`, `Platform`, `Refactor`)
325	- **Module**: The affected module (optional, e.g., `Misc`, `Model`, `Worker`)
326	- **Description**: Brief description of the change
327	
328	**Examples:**
329	
330	- `[Doc][Misc] Update contribution guidelines`
331	- `[BugFix] Fix CPU binding logic`
332	- `[CI] Update image build workflow`
333	
334	### Pull Request Template
335	
336	When creating a PR, please follow the template in `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` and ensure the following sections are completed:
337	
338	> **Note**: The PR description will be automatically updated by GitHub Actions to include vLLM version info at the bottom. If you update the PR description via API or CLI, make sure to preserve the `- vLLM version:` and `- vLLM main:` lines.
339	
340	- **What this PR does / why we need it?** - Clearly describe the changes and their purpose
341	- **Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?** - Indicate if there are any user-visible changes
342	- **How was this patch tested?** - Describe how you tested the changes. Examples:
343	    - Unit tests added/updated: list the test files
344	    - Manual testing: provide the test steps and commands
345	    - CI testing: indicate if only CI verification is needed
346	
347	---
348	
349	## Review Checklist
350	
351	Before merging, verify:
352	
353	### Code Quality
354	
355	- [ ] Code follows style guidelines (naming, imports, no magic numbers)
356	- [ ] No global state added without justification
357	- [ ] Patching pattern used correctly (if applicable)
358	- [ ] No direct model file additions
359	
360	### Testing
361	
362	- [ ] New tests added for new functionality (`tests/ut/` or `tests/e2e/`)
363	- [ ] Existing tests pass
364	- [ ] NPU-specific tests verified on actual hardware
365	- [ ] Performance benchmarks included where applicable
366	
367	### Documentation
368	
369	- [ ] Environment variables documented
370	- [ ] Public APIs documented
371	- [ ] User-facing changes reflected in docs
372	
373	### NPU Considerations
374	
375	- [ ] `tensor.item()` usage reviewed for performance impact
376	- [ ] No unnecessary CPU-NPU transfers in hot paths
377	- [ ] Memory usage verified on NPU hardware
378	
379	### Commit and PR
380	
381	- [ ] Commit messages are clear and descriptive, following Conventional Commits format
382	- [ ] **All commits are signed off** (`git commit -s`)
383	- [ ] PR is created from your fork repository, not directly from the main repository
384	- [ ] PR description is complete, following the PR template
385	- [ ] All review comments addressed
386	
387	---
388	
389	## Quick Start for Contributors
390	
391	1. Install development dependencies: `pip install -e .[dev]`
392	2. Run tests: `pytest tests/`
393	3. Check linting: `ruff check vllm_ascend/`
394	4. Format code: `ruff format vllm_ascend/`
395	5. Make your changes following guidelines in this document
396	6. Add tests for new behavior
397	7. Run full test suite before committing
398	8. Commit with sign-off: `git commit -s`
399	9. Run linting check before pushing:
400	   ```bash
401	   bash format.sh ci
402	   ```
403	   > **Note**: This check is required for **all file types**, including markdown files. If `markdownlint` modifies files, re-add them with `git add` and commit again.
404	10. Push to your fork repository (NOT the main repository):
405	
406	   ```bash
407	   git remote add myfork https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/vllm-ascend.git
408	   git push -u myfork your-branch-name
409	   ```
410	
411	11. Create a PR from your fork to the main repository with clear description
412	
413	---
414	
415	## References
416	
417	- [vLLM Hardware Plugin RFC](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/11162)
418	- [Documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/)
419	- [Contributors Guide](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/community/contributors.html)
420

This document provides instructions for contributors to the vLLM Ascend project. Please read and follow these guidelines to ensure code quality, maintainability, and consistency.

---

## Table of Contents

- [Setup and Environment](#setup-and-environment)
    - [Environment Variables](#environment-variables)

    - [Documentation](#documentation)
    - [NPU Considerations](#npu-considerations)
    - [Commit and PR](#commit-and-pr)
- [Quick Start for Contributors](#quick-start-for-contributors)
- [References](#references)

---

## Setup and Environment

### Environment Variables

All environment variables must be defined in `vllm_ascend/envs.py` using the centralized `env_variables` dictionary.

**Requirements:**

- Add documentation for each environment variable in the `env_variables` dict comment
- Specify default values and valid ranges
- Indicate whether the variable is sensitive (credentials, keys)

**Example:**

```python
import os

env_variables = {
    "VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_NZ": lambda: int(os.getenv("VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_NZ", 1)),
    # ...
}
```

**Never**: Hardcode environment variable names throughout the codebase. Reference them from the central module using `from vllm_ascend import envs`.

### Environment Variable Review Requirement

**Strict Review Required**: All new environment variables must undergo code review.

Reviewers must verify:

- The variable name follows the `VLLM_ASCEND_*` naming convention
- Default value is appropriate for all supported hardware
- Documentation is added to the `env_variables` dict
- The variable is used in a performance-critical path

---

## Testing

### Unit and System Tests

**Requirement**: All new functionality requires corresponding tests.

- **Unit Tests (UT)**: Located in `tests/ut/`, cover core logic, edge cases, and error conditions
- **System Tests (ST)**: Located in `tests/e2e/`, verify end-to-end behavior and integration points
- **Nightly Tests**: Include benchmarks for NPU-specific code paths in `tests/e2e/nightly/`

**Test Coverage Guidelines:**

- New features: Tests must cover happy path and failure modes
- Bug fixes: Tests must include a regression test for the bug
- Performance-critical code: Include benchmarks and performance regression tests

### Running Tests

```bash


# Run specific unit test file
pytest -sv tests/ut/ops/test_prepare_finalize.py

# Run specific unit test
pytest -sv tests/ut/ops/test_prepare_finalize.py::test_prepare_inputs

# Run NPU-specific tests (requires NPU hardware)
pytest -sv tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/aclgraph/test_aclgraph_accuracy.py::test_default_full_and_piecewise_res_consistency
```

**Requirement**: Run all tests locally before requesting review. Verify tests pass on NPU hardware for NPU-specific changes.

---

## Code Style

### Python Conventions

- **Imports**: All imports at the top of the file. Valid exceptions:
    - Circular imports (use inline imports)
    - Lazy loading for worker/isolation processes
    - Type-checking imports wrapped in `if TYPE_CHECKING:`

- **Global Variables**: Avoid new global variables. Pass dependencies explicitly through function parameters.

    **Allowed:**
    - Constants named `ALL_UPPER_CASE` (e.g., `MAX_BATCH_SIZE` in `envs.py`)
    - Immutable configuration objects

    **Requires Approval:**
    - Any new mutable global state

- **No Magic Numbers**: Use named constants with descriptive names:

    ```python
    # Bad
    if seq_len > 2048: ...

    # Good
    MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH = 2048
    if seq_len > MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH: ...
    ```

- **Descriptive Naming**: Use names that describe functionality, not implementation details.

    ```python
    # Bad
    is_deepseek_v3_r1
    flag1
    tmp_var

    # Good
    supports_dynamic_temperature
    uses_speculative_decoding
    ```

### Naming Conventions

- **Classes**: `PascalCase` (e.g., `NPUModelRunner`, `AscendSampler`, `ACLGraphManager`)
- **Functions/Methods**: `snake_case` (e.g., `forward_pass`, `compute_attention`)
- **Constants**: `ALL_UPPER_CASE` (e.g., `MAX_BATCH_SIZE`, `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_NZ`)
- **Variables**: `snake_case` (e.g., `token_ids`, `sequence_lengths`)

---

## NPU-Specific Considerations

### Tensor item() Operations

**Warning**: `tensor.item()` operations cause synchronization overhead on NPU when the `tensor` is on device.

If the `tensor` is a device tensor, calling `item()` will triggers a synchronous data transfer from NPU to CPU. This can severely degrade performance in hot paths, causing `AsyncScheduler` to block here.

**Review Requirements:**

1. Profile performance impact before merging
2. Consider alternative patterns:
    - Keep values on device when possible
    - Batch operations to reduce sync frequency
    - Use device-side operations (e.g., `torch.argmax`, `torch.sum`)
3. Document when `item()` is unavoidable (e.g., logging, conditional logic)

**Example Patterns:**

```python
# Bad: In hot loop - causes sync per iteration
for tensor in tensors:
    value = tensor.item()

# Better: Batch operations - single sync
values = [t.item() for t in tensors]  # Single batch sync

# Good: Keep on device when possible
max_value = torch.max(tensor)  # No sync needed
if max_value > threshold:  # Comparison can stay on device
    ...
```

### Memory and Performance

Additional NPU-specific best practices:

- Avoid CPU-NPU memory transfers in hot paths
- Prefer in-place operations where safe (e.g., `x.add_()`, `x.mul_()`)
- Monitor memory fragmentation, especially for long-running processes
- Test with realistic workloads on actual NPU hardware (Ascend 910B/C)

---

## Model and Plugin Architecture

### vLLM Ascend Plugin Architecture

vLLM Ascend is a **hardware plugin** that integrates with upstream vLLM via the pluggable hardware interface. It does not add new model files directly.

**Required Pattern**: Model-specific functionality should be implemented via:

1. **Patching** (in `vllm_ascend/patch/`):
    - `vllm_ascend/patch/platform/` - Platform-level patches (distributed, scheduling)
    - `vllm_ascend/patch/worker/` - Worker-level patches (model-specific behavior)
    - Example: `patch_deepseek.py` modifies upstream Deepseek model behavior
    - Patch is not the best solution for all cases. Use it when necessary.

2. **Inheritance**:
    - `NPUModelRunner(GPUModelRunner)` - Extend vLLM model runner with NPU-specific behavior
    - `AscendSampler` - Extend vLLM sampler with NPU-specific operations
    - Add NPU-specific components via composition (e.g., `AclGraphManager`)
    - Custom Operators - NPU-specific custom operators (e.g., `AscendRMSNorm`)

3. **External upstream contributions** where appropriate

### Patching Requirement

**Strict Review Required**: All new patches must undergo thorough architectural review.

Reviewers must verify:

- The patch targets the correct upstream component
- The patch is minimal and focused
- Performance implications are understood
- A long-term plan exists for upstream contribution

**Example Patch Pattern:**

```python
# vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_deepseek.py
from vllm.model_executor.models.deepseek_v2 import DeepseekV2Model

def forward(self, input_ids, positions, ...):
    # NPU-specific forward implementation
    ...

DeepseekV2Model.forward = forward  # Patch upstream class
```

### Model Runner Changes

**Strict Review Required**: All new behaviors added to `model_runner` must undergo thorough architectural review.

Reviewers must verify:

- The necessity of the new behavior (why can't this be in a patch?)
- Performance implications on NPU hardware
- Compatibility with existing model implementations
- Long-term maintainability and test coverage

**NPU Model Runner Files:**

- `vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py` - vLLM v1 model runner
- `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py` - vLLM v2 model runner
- `vllm_ascend/_310p/model_runner_310p.py` - Ascend 310P model runner

---

## Commit Messages and Pull Requests

### Commit Message Format

Follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format and **must include a sign-off**:

```bash
git commit -s -m "<type>: <summary>" -m "<body - explaining what changed and why>"
```

Or using the full message format:

```txt
<type>: <summary>

<body - explaining what changed and why>

Signed-off-by: Your Name <your.email@example.com>
```

**Valid Types**: `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `refactor`, `test`, `docs`, `chore`

**Good Examples:**

```txt
feat(npu): add flash attention support for Ascend CANN

- Implements FlashAttention-2 kernel for NPU backend
- Reduces memory usage by 30% compared to baseline

fix(model_runner): correct padding token handling

- Fixes token padding that caused incorrect attention masks
- Addresses issue #1234

perf: avoid CPU-NPU sync in attention computation

- Inline computation to avoid tensor.item() calls
- Improves throughput by 15%
```

**Bad Examples:**

```txt
fix bug
add feature
update code
```

### Pull Request Title Format

PR titles should follow the format: `[Type][Module] Description`

- **Type**: The type of change (e.g., `CI`, `Doc`, `BugFix`, `Feat`, `Platform`, `Refactor`)
- **Module**: The affected module (optional, e.g., `Misc`, `Model`, `Worker`)
- **Description**: Brief description of the change

**Examples:**

- `[Doc][Misc] Update contribution guidelines`
- `[BugFix] Fix CPU binding logic`
- `[CI] Update image build workflow`

### Pull Request Template

When creating a PR, please follow the template in `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` and ensure the following sections are completed:

> **Note**: The PR description will be automatically updated by GitHub Actions to include vLLM version info at the bottom. If you update the PR description via API or CLI, make sure to preserve the `- vLLM version:` and `- vLLM main:` lines.

- **What this PR does / why we need it?** - Clearly describe the changes and their purpose
- **Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?** - Indicate if there are any user-visible changes
- **How was this patch tested?** - Describe how you tested the changes. Examples:
    - Unit tests added/updated: list the test files
    - Manual testing: provide the test steps and commands
    - CI testing: indicate if only CI verification is needed

---

## Review Checklist

Before merging, verify:

### Code Quality

- [ ] Code follows style guidelines (naming, imports, no magic numbers)
- [ ] No global state added without justification
- [ ] Patching pattern used correctly (if applicable)
- [ ] No direct model file additions

### Testing

- [ ] New tests added for new functionality (`tests/ut/` or `tests/e2e/`)
- [ ] Existing tests pass
- [ ] NPU-specific tests verified on actual hardware
- [ ] Performance benchmarks included where applicable

### Documentation

- [ ] Environment variables documented
- [ ] Public APIs documented
- [ ] User-facing changes reflected in docs

### NPU Considerations

- [ ] `tensor.item()` usage reviewed for performance impact
- [ ] No unnecessary CPU-NPU transfers in hot paths
- [ ] Memory usage verified on NPU hardware

### Commit and PR

- [ ] Commit messages are clear and descriptive, following Conventional Commits format
- [ ] **All commits are signed off** (`git commit -s`)
- [ ] PR is created from your fork repository, not directly from the main repository
- [ ] PR description is complete, following the PR template
- [ ] All review comments addressed

---

## Quick Start for Contributors

1. Install development dependencies: `pip install -e .[dev]`
2. Run tests: `pytest tests/`
3. Check linting: `ruff check vllm_ascend/`
4. Format code: `ruff format vllm_ascend/`
5. Make your changes following guidelines in this document
6. Add tests for new behavior
7. Run full test suite before committing
8. Commit with sign-off: `git commit -s`
9. Run linting check before pushing:
   ```bash
   bash format.sh ci
   ```
   > **Note**: This check is required for **all file types**, including markdown files. If `markdownlint` modifies files, re-add them with `git add` and commit again.
10. Push to your fork repository (NOT the main repository):

   ```bash
   git remote add myfork https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/vllm-ascend.git
   git push -u myfork your-branch-name
   ```

11. Create a PR from your fork to the main repository with clear description

---

- [vLLM Hardware Plugin RFC](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/11162)
- [Documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/)
- [Contributors Guide](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/community/contributors.html)

"""Utility functions for expert offload initialization."""

import torch


def init_expert_offload_config(offload_config, num_experts: int):
    """Prepare pre-super().__init__() expert offload setup.

    Builds an expert_map_offload that the upstream layer.py hook reads
    to shrink the device weight and skip loading cold experts.

    Args:
        offload_config: ExpertOffloadConfig instance from AscendConfig.
        num_experts: Total routed expert count from model config.

    Returns:
        (enable: bool, expert_map_offload: torch.Tensor | None)
    """
    enable = (offload_config.expert_offload
              and offload_config.num_device_experts > 0
              and offload_config.num_device_experts < num_experts)
    if not enable:
        return False, None

    ndev = offload_config.num_device_experts
    emap = torch.full((num_experts,), -1, dtype=torch.int32)
    emap[:ndev] = torch.arange(ndev, dtype=torch.int32)
    return True, emap


def init_log2phy_for_offload(global_num_experts: int, num_device_experts: int):
    """Initialize the forward-pass log2phy mapping table."""
    log2phy = torch.arange(global_num_experts, dtype=torch.int32, device='npu')
    log2phy[num_device_experts:].fill_(-1)
    return log2phy

class LRCExpertCachePolicy:
    """Online approximation of SCH using recent frequency and EMA hotness.

    The policy is intentionally CPU-only. ExpertOffloadManager owns the actual
    CPU-to-NPU copies; this class only decides which resident expert should be
    evicted when a miss needs a device slot.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        num_layers: int,
        num_experts: int,
        cache_size: int,
        topk: int,
        recent_window: int = 32,
        ema_beta: float = 0.9,
        recent_weight: float = 1.0,
        ema_weight: float = 0.5,
        router_weight: float = 0.3,
        age_weight: float = 0.01,
    ) -> None:
        if num_layers < 1:
            raise ValueError("num_layers must be >= 1")
        if num_experts < 1:
            raise ValueError("num_experts must be >= 1")
        if cache_size < 1:
            raise ValueError("cache_size must be >= 1")
        if topk < 1:
            raise ValueError("topk must be >= 1")
        if recent_window < 1:
            raise ValueError("recent_window must be >= 1")
        if not 0.0 <= ema_beta < 1.0:
            raise ValueError("ema_beta must be in [0, 1)")

        self.num_experts = num_experts
        self.cache_size = cache_size
        self.topk = topk
        self.recent_window = recent_window
        self.ema_beta = ema_beta
        self.recent_weight = recent_weight
        self.ema_weight = ema_weight
        self.router_weight = router_weight
        self.age_weight = age_weight

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Overview

Multi-repo workspace for developing **MoE expert weight offloading** on vLLM-Ascend (Huawei Ascend NPU). The primary development happens in `vllm-ascend/`; `vllm/` is an upstream vLLM reference copy used for understanding APIs and debugging.

- **vllm/** — upstream vLLM (pinned to a dev branch with MoE offload support, currently on `moe_offload_support_dsv4` commit)
- **vllm-ascend/** — vLLM Ascend hardware plugin; active development happens here
- **scripts/run.sh** — example launch script for serving DeepSeek V4 with expert offloading on Ascend NPU

## Key architecture

### Expert Offloading (`vllm_ascend/expert_offload/`)

The core feature being developed. MoE models have many experts (e.g., 128) that don't fit on NPU memory, so weights are stored on CPU and paged to NPU at runtime based on routing decisions.

- **`ExpertOffloadManager`** (`expert_offload_manager.py`) — singleton that stores all expert weights on pinned CPU memory, paging `num_device_experts` experts to NPU. Owns CPU→NPU copy streams (load stream, prefetch stream). Manages prefill pools (round-robin shared across `num_device_layers` layers) and decode paging via cache policy.
- **`LRCExpertCachePolicy`** (`lrc_policy.py`) — Local-Routing-Consistency eviction policy. CPU-only online approximation of SCH using recent routing frequency, EMA hotness, router scores, and age to decide which resident expert to evict on a cache miss.
- **`utils.py`** — `init_expert_offload_config()` (generates `expert_map_offload`) and `init_log2phy_for_offload()` called during model init.
- **`ExpertOffloadConfig`** (in `ascend_config.py:775`) — driven by `--additional-config '{"expert_offload_config": {...}}'` passed to `vllm serve`. Key knobs: `num_device_experts`, `num_device_layers`, `cache_policy_enabled`, `expert_prefetch_enabled`.

### Prefetch Offloader (`vllm_ascend/model_executor/offloader/prefetch.py`)

NPU port of upstream `PrefetchOffloader`. Uses `torch.npu.*` APIs to asynchronously copy model parameters between NPU and CPU/pinned memory via a dedicated copy stream. Supports next-layer prefetch on a background thread (`_prefetch_thread`) so H2D copies never block the forward pass.

### Model support (`vllm_ascend/models/`)

- **`deepseek_v4.py`** — DeepSeek V4 model implementation with MoE-specific forward logic. Works with `ExpertOffloadManager`.
- **`layer/attention/`** — custom attention layer implementations for DeepSeek V4.
- Patching in `vllm_ascend/patch/worker/` modifies upstream model behavior at runtime (e.g., DeepSeek-specific patches).

### ACL Graph compilation (`vllm_ascend/compilation/`)

NPU graph capture/compilation infrastructure. `acl_graph.py` manages ACL graph lifecycle; `compiler_interface.py` interfaces with the Ascend compiler; `passes/` contains graph optimization passes.

### Plugin architecture (`vllm_ascend/patch/`)

vLLM-Ascend uses the upstream vLLM hardware-pluggable interface. NPU-specific behaviors are injected via:
1. **Patching** — monkey-patching upstream classes at import time (`patch/platform/`, `patch/worker/`)
2. **Inheritance** — `NPUModelRunner(GPUModelRunner)`, `AscendSampler`, etc.
3. **Custom ops** — compiled C++ kernels in `csrc/` (Moe ops, attention kernels, GMM)

## Environment variables

All env vars are centralized in `vllm_ascend/envs.py` in the `env_variables` dict. Follow the `VLLM_ASCEND_*` naming convention. Key ones:
- `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_NZ` — enable fractal NZ memory format
- `COMPILE_CUSTOM_KERNELS` — set to `0` only for non-NPU UT environments

## Build & Development

Work in `vllm-ascend/` for all changes.

```bash
# Build C++ extensions (from vllm-ascend/csrc/)
cd vllm-ascend && bash csrc/build.sh

# Install vllm-ascend in dev mode
cd vllm-ascend && pip install -e .

# Lint (uses pre-commit)
cd vllm-ascend && bash format.sh          # all hooks on all files
cd vllm-ascend && bash format.sh ci        # manual-stage hooks (including mypy)

# Run a specific unit test
cd vllm-ascend && pytest -sv tests/ut/path/to/test_file.py::test_name

# Run a specific E2E test (requires NPU hardware)
cd vllm-ascend && pytest -sv tests/e2e/path/to/test_file.py::test_name
```

## Commit conventions

- Conventional Commits: `<type>(<scope>): <summary>` with `Signed-off-by:` trailer (`git commit -s`)
- Valid types: `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `refactor`, `test`, `docs`, `chore`
- PR titles: `[Type][Module] Description` (e.g., `[Feat][Worker] Add next-layer prefetch`)

## Important constraints

- **Never hardcode env var names** — always import from `vllm_ascend.envs`
- **`tensor.item()` causes NPU→CPU sync** — avoid in hot paths; batch or keep on device
- **NPU uses fractal NZ format** (`ACL_FORMAT_FRACTAL_NZ`) for weight storage; transpose happens in `process_weights_after_loading()`
- **Expert offload uses pinned CPU memory** — all CPU-side expert weight buffers are `pin_memory=True`
- **The prefetch thread writes to NPU from a background thread** — NPU streams and events coordinate with the main forward thread; the `_prefetch_state_lock` protects shared state
- **C++ kernels in `csrc/`** are compiled via `csrc/build.sh` with CMake; custom MoE ops (`AscendFusedMoE`), attention kernels, and batch matmul ops live there
- **vllm/** should generally not be modified directly; changes flow upstream via PRs to vllm-project/vllm

- **vllm/** — upstream vLLM (pinned to a dev branch with MoE offload support, currently on `moe_offload_support_dsv4` commit)
- **vllm-ascend/** — vLLM Ascend hardware plugin; active development happens here
- **scripts/run.sh** — example launch script for serving DeepSeek V4 with expert offloading on Ascend NPU

> **Read `vllm-ascend/AGENTS.md`** before any contribution. It is the authoritative contributor guide (env-var rules, NPU hot-path constraints, patching/inheritance patterns, commit & PR format, review checklists). The conventions there are stricter than what's summarized here.

## Key architecture

### Expert Offloading (`vllm_ascend/expert_offload/`)

The core feature being developed. MoE models have many experts (e.g., 128) that don't fit on NPU memory, so weights are stored on CPU and paged to NPU at runtime based on routing decisions.

- **`ExpertOffloadManager`** (`expert_offload_manager.py`) — singleton that stores all expert weights on pinned CPU memory, paging `num_device_experts` experts to NPU. Owns CPU→NPU copy streams (load stream, prefetch stream). Manages prefill pools (round-robin shared across `num_device_layers` layers) and decode paging via cache policy.
- **`LRCExpertCachePolicy`** (`lrc_policy.py`) — Local-Routing-Consistency eviction policy. CPU-only online approximation of SCH using recent routing frequency, EMA hotness, router scores, and age to decide which resident expert to evict on a cache miss.
- **`utils.py`** — `init_expert_offload_config()` (generates `expert_map_offload`) and `init_log2phy_for_offload()` called during model init.
- **`ExpertOffloadConfig`** (in `ascend_config.py:775`) — driven by `--additional-config '{"expert_offload_config": {...}}'` passed to `vllm serve`. Key knobs: `num_device_experts`, `num_device_layers`, `cache_policy_enabled`, `expert_prefetch_enabled`.

### Prefetch Offloader (`vllm_ascend/model_executor/offloader/prefetch.py`)

NPU port of upstream `PrefetchOffloader`. Uses `torch.npu.*` APIs to asynchronously copy model parameters between NPU and CPU/pinned memory via a dedicated copy stream. Supports next-layer prefetch on a background thread (`_prefetch_thread`) so H2D copies never block the forward pass.

### Model support (`vllm_ascend/models/`)

- **`deepseek_v4.py`** — DeepSeek V4 model implementation with MoE-specific forward logic. Works with `ExpertOffloadManager`.
- **`layer/attention/`** — custom attention layer implementations for DeepSeek V4.
- Patching in `vllm_ascend/patch/worker/` modifies upstream model behavior at runtime (e.g., DeepSeek-specific patches).

### ACL Graph compilation (`vllm_ascend/compilation/`)

NPU graph capture/compilation infrastructure. `acl_graph.py` manages ACL graph lifecycle; `compiler_interface.py` interfaces with the Ascend compiler; `passes/` contains graph optimization passes.

### Plugin architecture (`vllm_ascend/patch/`)

vLLM-Ascend uses the upstream vLLM hardware-pluggable interface. NPU-specific behaviors are injected via:
1. **Patching** — monkey-patching upstream classes at import time (`patch/platform/`, `patch/worker/`)
2. **Inheritance** — `NPUModelRunner(GPUModelRunner)`, `AscendSampler`, etc.
3. **Custom ops** — compiled C++ kernels in `csrc/` (Moe ops, attention kernels, GMM)

## Environment variables

All env vars are centralized in `vllm_ascend/envs.py` in the `env_variables` dict. Follow the `VLLM_ASCEND_*` naming convention. Key ones:
- `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_NZ` — enable fractal NZ memory format
- `COMPILE_CUSTOM_KERNELS` — set to `0` only for non-NPU UT environments

## Build & Development

Work in `vllm-ascend/` for all changes.

```bash
# Build C++ extensions (from vllm-ascend/csrc/)
cd vllm-ascend && bash csrc/build.sh

# Install vllm-ascend in dev mode
cd vllm-ascend && pip install -e .

# Lint (uses pre-commit)
cd vllm-ascend && bash format.sh          # all hooks on all files
cd vllm-ascend && bash format.sh ci        # manual-stage hooks (including mypy)

# Run a specific unit test
cd vllm-ascend && pytest -sv tests/ut/path/to/test_file.py::test_name

# Run a specific E2E test (requires NPU hardware)
cd vllm-ascend && pytest -sv tests/e2e/path/to/test_file.py::test_name
```

## Commit conventions

- Conventional Commits: `<type>(<scope>): <summary>` with `Signed-off-by:` trailer (`git commit -s`)
- Valid types: `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `refactor`, `test`, `docs`, `chore`
- PR titles: `[Type][Module] Description` (e.g., `[Feat][Worker] Add next-layer prefetch`)

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Overview

Multi-repo workspace for developing **MoE expert weight offloading** on vLLM-Ascend (Huawei Ascend NPU). The primary development happens in `vllm-ascend/`; `vllm/` is an upstream vLLM reference copy used for understanding APIs and debugging.

- **vllm/** — upstream vLLM (pinned to a dev branch with MoE offload support, currently on `moe_offload_support_dsv4` commit)
- **vllm-ascend/** — vLLM Ascend hardware plugin; active development happens here
- **scripts/run.sh** — example launch script for serving DeepSeek V4 with expert offloading on Ascend NPU

> **Read `vllm-ascend/AGENTS.md`** before any contribution. It is the authoritative contributor guide (env-var rules, NPU hot-path constraints, patching/inheritance patterns, commit & PR format, review checklists). The conventions there are stricter than what's summarized here.

## Key architecture

### Expert Offloading (`vllm_ascend/expert_offload/`)

The core feature being developed. MoE models have many experts (e.g., 128) that don't fit on NPU memory, so weights are stored on CPU and paged to NPU at runtime based on routing decisions.

- **`ExpertOffloadManager`** (`expert_offload_manager.py`) — process-wide singleton (access via `ExpertOffloadManager.get_instance()`, set in `__init__`) that stores all expert weights on pinned CPU memory, paging `num_device_experts` experts to NPU. Owns CPU→NPU copy streams (`load_stream`, `_prefetch_stream`) and the background `_prefetch_thread` (guarded by `_prefetch_state_lock`) that issues next-expert H2D copies off the forward path. Manages prefill pools (round-robin shared across `num_device_layers` layers) and decode paging via cache policy.
- **`LRCExpertCachePolicy`** (`lrc_policy.py`) — Local-Routing-Consistency eviction policy. CPU-only online approximation of SCH using recent routing frequency, EMA hotness, router scores, and age to decide which resident expert to evict on a cache miss.
- **`utils.py`** — `init_expert_offload_config()` (generates `expert_map_offload`) and `init_log2phy_for_offload()` called during model init.
- **`ExpertOffloadConfig`** (in `ascend_config.py:775`) — driven by `--additional-config '{"expert_offload_config": {...}}'` passed to `vllm serve`. Key knobs: `expert_offload` (master switch), `num_device_experts` (default 32), `num_device_layers` (default 2), `cache_policy_enabled`, `expert_prefetch_enabled`, `cache_debug_log_updates`. The `cache_*` knobs (`cache_recent_window`, `cache_ema_beta`, `cache_recent_weight`, `cache_ema_weight`, `cache_router_weight`, `cache_age_weight`) map 1:1 onto `LRCExpertCachePolicy.__init__`.

### Prefetch Offloader (`vllm_ascend/model_executor/offloader/prefetch.py`)

Generic NPU port of upstream vLLM's `PrefetchOffloader` (`NPUPrefetchOffloader`). It offloads **whole module/layer parameters** (not individual experts) between NPU and CPU/pinned memory over a dedicated `copy_stream` with a `StaticBufferPool`, reusing upstream's `_BaseParamOffloader`. Enabled via `--safetensors-load-strategy prefetch`.

> Note: the background-thread **expert** prefetch (`_prefetch_thread`, `_prefetch_stream`, `_prefetch_state_lock`) belongs to `ExpertOffloadManager`, **not** this module. Don't conflate the two — `prefetch.py` is about layer weights; expert paging is the offload manager.

### Model support (`vllm_ascend/models/`)

- **`deepseek_v4.py`** — DeepSeek V4 model implementation with MoE-specific forward logic. Works with `ExpertOffloadManager`.
- **`layer/attention/`** — custom attention layer implementations for DeepSeek V4.
- Patching in `vllm_ascend/patch/worker/` modifies upstream model behavior at runtime (e.g., DeepSeek-specific patches).

### ACL Graph compilation (`vllm_ascend/compilation/`)

NPU graph capture/compilation infrastructure. `acl_graph.py` manages ACL graph lifecycle; `compiler_interface.py` interfaces with the Ascend compiler; `passes/` contains graph optimization passes.

### Plugin architecture (`vllm_ascend/patch/`)

vLLM-Ascend uses the upstream vLLM hardware-pluggable interface. NPU-specific behaviors are injected via:
1. **Patching** — monkey-patching upstream classes at import time (`patch/platform/`, `patch/worker/`)
2. **Inheritance** — `NPUModelRunner(GPUModelRunner)`, `AscendSampler`, etc.
3. **Custom ops** — compiled C++ kernels in `csrc/` (Moe ops, attention kernels, GMM)

## Environment variables

All env vars are centralized in `vllm_ascend/envs.py` in the `env_variables` dict. Follow the `VLLM_ASCEND_*` naming convention. Key ones:
- `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_NZ` — enable fractal NZ memory format
- `COMPILE_CUSTOM_KERNELS` — set to `0` only for non-NPU UT environments

## Build & Development

Work in `vllm-ascend/` for all changes.

```bash
# Build C++ extensions (from vllm-ascend/csrc/)
cd vllm-ascend && bash csrc/build.sh

# Install vllm-ascend in dev mode
cd vllm-ascend && pip install -e .

# Lint (uses pre-commit)
cd vllm-ascend && bash format.sh          # all hooks on all files
cd vllm-ascend && bash format.sh ci        # manual-stage hooks (including mypy)

# Run a specific unit test
cd vllm-ascend && pytest -sv tests/ut/path/to/test_file.py::test_name

# Run a specific E2E test (requires NPU hardware)
cd vllm-ascend && pytest -sv tests/e2e/path/to/test_file.py::test_name
```

## Commit conventions

- Conventional Commits: `<type>(<scope>): <summary>` with `Signed-off-by:` trailer (`git commit -s`)
- Valid types: `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `refactor`, `test`, `docs`, `chore`
- PR titles: `[Type][Module] Description` (e.g., `[Feat][Worker] Add next-layer prefetch`)

## Important constraints

- **Never hardcode env var names** — always import from `vllm_ascend.envs`
- **`tensor.item()` causes NPU→CPU sync** — avoid in hot paths; batch or keep on device
- **NPU uses fractal NZ format** (`ACL_FORMAT_FRACTAL_NZ`) for weight storage; transpose happens in `process_weights_after_loading()`
- **Expert offload uses pinned CPU memory** — all CPU-side expert weight buffers are `pin_memory=True`
- **The prefetch thread writes to NPU from a background thread** — NPU streams and events coordinate with the main forward thread; the `_prefetch_state_lock` protects shared state
- **C++ kernels in `csrc/`** are compiled via `csrc/build.sh` with CMake; custom MoE ops (`AscendFusedMoE`), attention kernels, and batch matmul ops live there
- **vllm/** should generally not be modified directly; changes flow upstream via PRs to vllm-project/vllm

+- `--quantization ascend` — native Ascend W8A8 path; weights load in fractal NZ format.
+- `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` — ACL graph captures decode only (offload paging is not graph-safe in prefill).

    refactor(expert_offload): remove _pending_weights/_pending_scales lazy init
    
    Replace the lazy-init pattern (where CPU buffers were allocated after
    weight loading, requiring _pending_* dicts as temporary storage) with
    per-layer buffer allocation during AscendFusedMoE.__init__().

    - Add init_layer_cpu_buffers() called from AscendFusedMoE.__init__
      to allocate per-layer CPU weight + scale/offset buffers early
    - Add _load_scale_shard() with lightweight _scale_shard_temp for
      w13 scale/offset w1/w3 shard assembly
    - Add _finalize_offload() consolidating NZ conversion, cache policy
      init, prefill pool creation, and gate weight registration
    - Remove _pending_weights, _pending_scales, _drain_pending_*,
      register_moe_layer(), maybe_create_scale_buffers(), create_weights()
    - Simplify load_w13()/load_w2() to always copy directly to CPU buffer
    - Use logical dimensions (layer.hidden_size, intermediate_size)
      instead of device tensor shapes for CPU buffer allocation to
      avoid W8A8 pre-transpose layout confusion
    - Add .reshape() at all scale/offset copy sites to handle
      pre-flatten vs post-flatten shape mismatch
    - Simplify _register_offload_layers() to _finalize_offload_setup()
      in model_runner_v1.py

Now let me look at the second commit (d783c7a - prefetch thread), and also the fused_moe.py and model_runner_v1.py changes in commit 1. Let me also look at the current full state of the manager to understand the load path. Let me get the other diffs and the current code.

The key things I'm noticing so far in commit 93ffbab:

1. **`_byte_sizes_set` is a class attribute** (`_byte_sizes_set: bool = False`) defined inside the class body but it's being used as instance state via `self._byte_sizes_set`. This is a classic Python bug: class-level mutable/bool flag accessed via self. Actually bool is immutable so `self._byte_sizes_set = True` creates an instance attribute, which is fine, but defining it at class level is misleading and it's a shared default. Minor smell.

2. The `process_weights_after_loading()` is called from `_finalize_offload` after all weights are loaded. This is the NZ conversion. Let me look at it — it's the big perf bottleneck candidate. NZ format conversion is expensive.

3. The refactor removed lazy init and now allocates CPU buffers upfront. The `.reshape()` added at every copy site is a band-aid for shape mismatch — there are MANY `.reshape()` calls added. This is a code smell: the reshape was added defensively to "handle pre-flatten vs post-flatten shape mismatch". This suggests the buffer shapes and the copy target shapes don't align cleanly, which means extra metadata/validation work, though reshape itself is cheap (no data copy). Still, the proliferation of `.reshape(...)` everywhere is ugly.

   - `init_device_experts()` pages `num_device_experts` to NPU.

      instead of device tensor shapes for CPU buffer allocation to
      avoid W8A8 pre-transpose layout confusion
    - Add .reshape() at all scale/offset copy sites to handle
      pre-flatten vs post-flatten shape mismatch

if self.offload_config.expert_prefetch_enabled:
            self.register_gate_weights(model)

    def process_weights_after_loading(self):
        first_w13 = self.w13_weights_cpu[0][0]
        first_w2 = self.w2_weights_cpu[0][0]
        self.w13_expert_size_bytes = first_w13.nelement() * first_w13.element_size()
        self.w2_expert_size_bytes = first_w2.nelement() * first_w2.element_size()
        if first_w13.dtype != torch.int8:
            return
        # for w8a8, npu weight tensor is cast to NZ format,
        # so we also store NZ format weight in weights_cpu,
        # and copy_ tensor's underlying storage instead of tensor itself
        # to avoid implicit format conversion during h2d.
        num_moe_layers = len(self.w13_weights_cpu)
        num_experts = len(self.w13_weights_cpu[0])
        for layer_id in range(num_moe_layers):
            w13 = torch.stack(self.w13_weights_cpu[layer_id]).to('npu')
            w13_nz = torch_npu.npu_format_cast(w13, ACL_FORMAT_FRACTAL_NZ)
            w13_nz_storage = w13_nz.untyped_storage()
            w2 = torch.stack(self.w2_weights_cpu[layer_id]).to('npu')
            w2_nz = torch_npu.npu_format_cast(w2, ACL_FORMAT_FRACTAL_NZ)
            w2_nz_storage = w2_nz.untyped_storage()
            for expert_id in range(num_experts):
                self.w13_weights_cpu[layer_id][expert_id].untyped_storage().copy_(
                    w13_nz_storage[expert_id * self.w13_expert_size_bytes : (expert_id + 1) * self.w13_expert_size_bytes]
                )
                self.w2_weights_cpu[layer_id][expert_id].untyped_storage().copy_(
                    w2_nz_storage[expert_id * self.w2_expert_size_bytes : (expert_id + 1) * self.w2_expert_size_bytes]
                )

    def register_gate_weights(self, model):
        """Store fp32 CPU copies of gate.weight for each MoE layer.

        Called from _finalize_offload() after all MoE layers are
        registered.  The gate weights are used by predict_next_layer_experts()
        to predict which experts the next layer will need.
        """
        from vllm_ascend.models.deepseek_v4 import DeepseekV4MoE
        moe_wrappers = [m for m in model.modules()
                        if isinstance(m, DeepseekV4MoE)]
        for wrapper in moe_wrappers:
            gate_cpu = wrapper.gate.weight.data.cpu().float().clone()
            self._gate_weights_cpu.append(gate_cpu)
        logger.info("[PREFETCH] registered gate weights for %d MoE layers",
                    len(self._gate_weights_cpu))

    def load_w13(self, layer_moe_idx: int, expert_id: int,
                 loaded_weight: torch.Tensor, shard_id: str):
        """Store w1/w3 shard to CPU buffer (with transpose to post format)."""
        cpu = self.w13_weights_cpu[layer_moe_idx][expert_id]
        intermed = cpu.shape[1] // 2
        w = loaded_weight.cpu()
        if shard_id == "w1":
            cpu[:, :intermed].copy_(w.t())
        elif shard_id == "w3":
            cpu[:, intermed: intermed + w.shape[0]].copy_(w.t())

    def load_w2(self, layer_moe_idx: int, expert_id: int,
                loaded_weight: torch.Tensor):
        """Store w2 weight to CPU buffer (with transpose to post format)."""
        self.w2_weights_cpu[layer_moe_idx][expert_id].copy_(loaded_weight.cpu().t())

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    #  Scale / offset helpers (quantized models only)                     #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def _load_scale_shard(self, layer_moe_idx: int, expert_id: int,
                          attr_name: str, shard_id: str,
                          loaded_weight: torch.Tensor):
        """Load a scale/offset shard into its CPU buffer.

        w13 scale/offset arrives as two shards (w1, w3) that must be
        concatenated along dim 0.  We stash the first-arriving shard in
        _scale_shard_temp and assemble when the second shard arrives.
        w2 scale/offset is a single shard — write directly.
        """
        if attr_name.startswith("w13_"):
            key = (layer_moe_idx, expert_id, attr_name)
            prev = self._scale_shard_temp.pop(key, None)
            if prev is not None:
                # Second shard — assemble and write
                if shard_id == "w1":
                    w1, w3 = loaded_weight.cpu(), prev
                else:
                    w1, w3 = prev, loaded_weight.cpu()
                target_dict = (self.scale_cpu_buffers if "scale" in attr_name
                               else self.offset_cpu_buffers)
                target = target_dict[attr_name][layer_moe_idx][expert_id]
                assembled = torch.cat([w1, w3], dim=0).reshape(target.shape)
                target.copy_(assembled)
            else:
                # First shard — stash
                self._scale_shard_temp[key] = loaded_weight.cpu()
        else:
            # w2 scale/offset — write directly
            target_dict = (self.scale_cpu_buffers if "scale" in attr_name
                           else self.offset_cpu_buffers)
            target = target_dict[attr_name][layer_moe_idx][expert_id]
            w_cpu = loaded_weight.cpu().reshape(target.shape)
            target.copy_(w_cpu)

    def init_device_experts(self):
        """Refresh derived fp32 scale after weight loading.

        Device experts are already loaded by the weight loader and
        process_weights_after_loading. Only refresh w13_weight_scale_fp32.
        """
        for i, layer in enumerate(self.moe_layers):
            ndev = min(self.num_device_experts, layer.w13_weight.shape[0])
            if hasattr(layer, 'w13_weight_scale_fp32'):
                for j in range(ndev):
                    layer.w13_weight_scale_fp32[j].copy_(
                        layer.w13_weight_scale.data[j].to(torch.float32))

    def create_prefill_pool(self):
        """Allocate prefill pool tensors on NPU with full expert count.

        Called from _finalize_offload() after decode buffers are set up.
        Creates ndl device tensors each holding all experts (e.g. 128).
        These are used when num_tokens > offload_threshold (large-batch
        prefill), loaded via full-overwrite in _prefill_load_layer.
        """
        if self._prefill_initialized:
            return
        if not self.moe_layers:
            return
        ndl = self.num_device_layers
        pool_layer = self.moe_layers[0]
        dev = pool_layer.w13_weight.device

content.thinking:
Now I've found the **key performance bottleneck**. Let me analyze `process_weights_after_loading()`:

```python
def process_weights_after_loading(self):
    first_w13 = self.w13_weights_cpu[0][0]
    first_w2 = self.w2_weights_cpu[0][0]
    self.w13_expert_size_bytes = first_w13.nelement() * first_w13.element_size()
    self.w2_expert_size_bytes = first_w2.nelement() * first_w2.element_size()
    if first_w13.dtype != torch.int8:
        return
    num_moe_layers = len(self.w13_weights_cpu)
    num_experts = len(self.w13_weights_cpu[0])
    for layer_id in range(num_moe_layers):
        w13 = torch.stack(self.w13_weights_cpu[layer_id]).to('npu')   # <-- STACKS all experts, copies CPU->NPU
        w13_nz = torch_npu.npu_format_cast(w13, ACL_FORMAT_FRACTAL_NZ)  # <-- NZ conversion on NPU
        w13_nz_storage = w13_nz.untyped_storage()
        w2 = torch.stack(self.w2_weights_cpu[layer_id]).to('npu')
        w2_nz = torch_npu.npu_format_cast(w2, ACL_FORMAT_FRACTAL_NZ)
        w2_nz_storage = w2_nz.untyped_storage()
        for expert_id in range(num_experts):
            self.w13_weights_cpu[layer_id][expert_id].untyped_storage().copy_(
                w13_nz_storage[expert_id * self.w13_expert_size_bytes : (expert_id + 1) * self.w13_expert_size_bytes]
            )   # <-- copies NZ-format NPU storage BACK to pinned CPU storage
            ...
```

This is the bottleneck. Here's what happens for EACH of the ~61 MoE layers:

1. `torch.stack(self.w13_weights_cpu[layer_id])` — creates a NEW tensor stacking 128 expert tensors along dim 0. This is a CPU memory allocation + copy of ALL expert weights for that layer. For DeepSeek V4, w13 is `[hidden, 2*intermediate]`. hidden=7168, intermediate=2048 (per partition, but with EP could be different). So per expert w13 ~ 7168 * 4096 bytes (int8) = ~29MB. ×128 experts ×61 layers... stack allocates ~3.7GB per layer then `.to('npu')` copies it to NPU.

2. `.to('npu')` — copies the whole stacked tensor to NPU (H2D). ~3.7GB per layer × 61 layers.

3. `npu_format_cast` to FRACTAL_NZ — this is the NZ conversion. It allocates a NEW NPU tensor in NZ format and does the conversion (NZ format is a 16x16 fractal tiling). This is computationally expensive AND allocates ~2x memory (NZ format has padding overhead, ~1.0x-1.125x but the conversion process needs scratch).

4. Then the inner loop copies the NZ-format storage **BACK to CPU pinned memory** for each expert. So it's NPU→CPU transfer of the NZ-converted data (~3.7GB per layer).

So the data movement is: CPU (stack) → NPU (H2D) → NZ convert on NPU → CPU (D2H). That's a LOT of data movement, all serialized layer by layer.

Wait — but WHY convert to NZ and store back on CPU? Because at runtime, the experts are paged CPU→NPU, and if the CPU copy is already in NZ format, the H2D copy won't trigger an implicit (slow) format conversion on the NPU side. That's the rationale in the comment: "we also store NZ format weight in weights_cpu, and copy_ tensor's underlying storage instead of tensor itself to avoid implicit format conversion during h2d."

But this is doing the conversion for ALL experts upfront during loading, even cold experts that may rarely be paged. For 128 experts × 61 layers that's a huge upfront cost. This is the 10-minute bottleneck almost certainly.

**Key insight**: Converting ALL experts to NZ format upfront at load time is the dominant cost. This is a load-time optimization trade-off: pay NZ conversion once at load (for all experts) vs. pay it on each page-in at runtime.

But actually — is NZ conversion even needed to be stored in CPU? Let me think. The alternative: store experts in normal (ND) format on CPU, and convert to NZ on-the-fly during page-in. But the comment says that triggers "implicit format conversion during h2d" which is slow. However, there might be a middle ground.

Actually, the bigger issue: this is serialized and single-threaded. Let me look at what can be parallelized.

Let me also check: is this NZ conversion done per-layer sequentially? Yes, the outer `for layer_id` loop is sequential. And it's on the default stream (no explicit stream context except the load_stream is not used here). Actually `npu_format_cast` runs on the default NPU stream. So each layer: H2D (blocks) → NZ cast (blocks) → D2H (blocks). Serial.

Now, the **10-minute** problem. Let me estimate:
- DeepSeek V4: Let me check the actual model dims. Actually this is "glm-5" served model but the path is v4_w8a8. DeepSeek V4 has 61 MoE layers, 128 experts (or 256 routed?). Let me not guess; the point is it's large.

Per layer:
- w13 stack: 128 × [hidden, 2*inter] int8. If hidden=7168, inter_per_partition=2048 (EP=1, 128 experts, but expert parallel). Actually with `--enable-expert-parallel` and TP=1, intermediate_size_per_partition = full intermediate / ... hmm. Let me just note it's big.

The total work is dominated by:
1. `torch.stack` (CPU copy, ~seconds per layer)
2. `.to('npu')` H2D (bandwidth limited, ~3.7GB at ~10GB/s PCIe = ~0.4s/layer... ×61 = ~24s. Not 10 min.)
3. `npu_format_cast` NZ — this is the expensive one. NZ conversion on NPU. For a [128, 7168, 4096] int8 tensor = 3.7GB. NZ conversion is memory-bandwidth heavy and allocates scratch. Could be several seconds per layer.
4. D2H back to CPU (~0.4s/layer ×61 = ~24s)

Hmm, that alone maybe 2-4 min. But there might be MORE. Let me reconsider — `torch.stack` is actually quite slow because it allocates and copies. And `npu_format_cast` might be doing a transpose too.

Actually, wait. There's a subtlety. The NZ format conversion `npu_format_cast` requires the NPU→ the result. But then copying the NZ **storage** back to CPU pinned memory via `.untyped_storage().copy_()` — this copy_ from NPU storage to CPU storage is a D2H transfer. But is it async? It's on the default stream without synchronization specified, but `untyped_storage().copy_()` between NPU and CPU... Actually `copy_` from a NPU tensor to a CPU tensor issues a D2H copy on the current stream.

The real issue: **everything is serial on one stream**, and there's a huge amount of redundant data movement (CPU→NPU→CPU round trip just to do format conversion).

**Alternative approaches to speed this up:**

1. **Do NZ conversion on CPU** (avoid the round-trip). `torch_npu` may not support CPU-side NZ cast, but if it does (or if we can do the fractal reformat in numpy/torch on CPU), we avoid H2D+NZ+D2H. This would be the biggest win.

2. **Parallelize across layers** — use multiple streams or threads so multiple layers' conversions overlap. Currently it's a serial loop.

3. **Convert only hot experts** — defer NZ conversion of cold experts to first page-in. But this complicates the runtime path.

4. **Avoid `torch.stack`** — instead of stacking 128 experts (which copies), allocate one contiguous buffer per layer from the start and load weights directly into it. Then a single `.to('npu')` without the stack copy. Actually the experts ARE separate tensors; stacking copies them. If we made `w13_weights_cpu[layer_id]` a single `[num_experts, ...]` tensor (or views into one storage), we'd skip the stack copy.

Actually, the most impactful and clean optimization:

**Option A: Make per-layer CPU buffers a single contiguous tensor, not a list of 128 separate tensors.**
- Currently `self.w13_weights_cpu[layer_id]` is a `list[Tensor]` of 128 tensors, each `pin_memory`.
- `torch.stack` then copies them into one contiguous tensor.
- If instead we allocate ONE tensor `[num_experts, hidden, 2*inter]` and have the list be views/slices, we skip the stack copy entirely. Then `.to('npu')` is a single transfer. And `npu_format_cast` operates on the single tensor.
- But the load path (`load_w13`) writes per-expert slices, which works fine with views into a contiguous buffer.
- Downstream code accesses `self.w13_weights_cpu[layer_id][expert_id]` — this still works as indexing into the contiguous tensor (returns a view). 

Actually wait — after NZ conversion, the storage is copied back per-expert into the individual tensors' storage. If they're views into one contiguous buffer, `untyped_storage().copy_()` per expert would write into the big buffer's storage at the right offset. That works but is fiddly. Alternatively, keep the big NZ storage directly.

**Option B: Overlap H2D / NZ-cast / D2H across layers using streams.**
- Pipeline: while layer N is doing D2H, layer N+1 does H2D, layer N+2 NZ-cast... This hides latency. Needs careful stream management.

**Option C: Check if NZ conversion can be done lazily / on fewer experts.**
- The prefill pool only needs `num_device_layers` worth (ndl copies of all experts). The decode path only needs `num_device_experts`. Cold experts only get NZ-converted when paged in. But the current code NZ-converts ALL experts because they might be needed.

    def _init_prefill_pool_data(self, dev, ntotal: int, ndl: int):
        """Load layer 0 weights into all prefill pool slots.

        Prefill pool tensors are already NZ-cast at this point (done in
        create_prefill_pool). Use simple per-expert copy_() — same pattern
        as the decode path's _update_weights.
        """
        has_scales = bool(self._prefill_w13_scale)
        has_offsets = bool(self._prefill_w13_offset)

        for slot in range(ndl):
            for eid in range(min(ntotal, len(self.w13_weights_cpu[0]))):
                self._prefill_w13[slot].untyped_storage()[eid * self.w13_expert_size_bytes : (eid + 1) * self.w13_expert_size_bytes].copy_(
                    self.w13_weights_cpu[0][eid].untyped_storage()
                )
                self._prefill_w2[slot].untyped_storage()[eid * self.w2_expert_size_bytes : (eid + 1) * self.w2_expert_size_bytes].copy_(
                    self.w2_weights_cpu[0][eid].untyped_storage()
                )

            # Initialize scale/offset buffers with layer 0 data (W8A8)
            if has_scales:
                for scale_name, prefill_list, cpu_buffers in [
                    ("w13_weight_scale", self._prefill_w13_scale, self.scale_cpu_buffers),
                    ("w2_weight_scale", self._prefill_w2_scale, self.scale_cpu_buffers),
                ]:
                    if (scale_name in cpu_buffers and
                            0 < len(cpu_buffers[scale_name])):
                        for eid in range(min(ntotal, len(cpu_buffers[scale_name][0]))):
                            prefill_list[slot][eid].copy_(
                                cpu_buffers[scale_name][0][eid]
                                .reshape(prefill_list[slot][eid].shape))
            if has_offsets:
                for offset_name, prefill_list, cpu_buffers in [
                    ("w13_weight_offset", self._prefill_w13_offset, self.offset_cpu_buffers),
                    ("w2_weight_offset", self._prefill_w2_offset, self.offset_cpu_buffers),
                ]:
                    if (offset_name in cpu_buffers and
                            0 < len(cpu_buffers[offset_name])):
                        for eid in range(min(ntotal, len(cpu_buffers[offset_name][0]))):
                            prefill_list[slot][eid].copy_(
                                cpu_buffers[offset_name][0][eid]
                                .reshape(prefill_list[slot][eid].shape))
            # Initialize fp32 scale (convert from scale)
            if has_scales and slot < len(self._prefill_w13_scale_fp32):
                for eid in range(min(ntotal, self._prefill_w13_scale[slot].shape[0])):
                    self._prefill_w13_scale_fp32[slot][eid].copy_(
                        self._prefill_w13_scale[slot][eid].to(torch.float32))

    def _prefill_load_layer(self, layer_idx: int, log2phy: torch.Tensor):
        """Load ALL experts for model layer layer_idx into the prefill pool.

        For W8A8: loads into normal-format scratch, then casts to NZ.
        For unquantized: loads directly into pool tensors via copy_().
        Full-overwrite into pool_slot = layer_idx % ndl.  No slot_owner
        tracking needed — log2phy is set to identity for prefill.
        """
        ndl = self.num_device_layers
        pool_slot = layer_idx % ndl
        dev = self._prefill_w13[pool_slot].device
        ntotal = self.num_total_experts
